requirements.requirement: node1 (VyOS) configured to run a DHCP server on the private network shared with node2 and node3
requirements.summary: eth1/enp8s0 identified as the second, unaddressed NIC common to all three nodes. node1's eth1 was statically assigned 10.10.10.1/24 and a Kea DHCPv4 shared-network 'PRIVATE' (subnet 10.10.10.0/24, pool 10.10.10.100-200, routers/name-server 10.10.10.1) was committed and saved to /config/config.boot. isc-kea-dhcp4-server was confirmed active, and Kea logs plus the rendered kea-dhcp4.conf, plus DHCPOFFER/DHCPACK entries for node2/node3 MACs, directly show the server issuing leases on eth1.

requirements.requirement: node2 and node3 configured to obtain their private-network address dynamically from node1 rather than a static assignment
requirements.summary: systemd-networkd configuration on both nodes (/etc/systemd/network/50-all-interfaces.network, Match Name=en*, DHCP=yes) applies to enp8s0 with no static override present. Live 'ip addr' output confirms 'dynamic' addresses 10.10.10.101 (node2) / 10.10.10.100 (node3) on enp8s0, and node1's Kea lease CSV records active leases with the correct MACs (later updated with hostnames node2/node3), directly demonstrating DHCP-assigned addressing rather than static configuration.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol: healthy baseline, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and recovered service/data/cluster state for node1, node2, node3
requirements.summary: For each node the trace shows: pre-restart boot_id and healthy state (node1 50503c5d with active eth1/Kea; node2 29011044 and node3 1e0cb179 with active dynamic leases); a scheduled reboot acknowledged locally; a bounded window of connection failures confirming the disruption; and a new boot_id post-restart (node1 66058e73, node2 2bbf9a82, node3 f09dde7c) matching the fixed after_executor snapshot. Recovery is directly observed: node1's eth1 address, Kea service, and saved config persisted; node2/node3 re-acquired dynamic DHCP leases from node1 on enp8s0, and node1's lease table shows both hosts with hostnames post-restart, confirming end-to-end cluster/service recovery.

overall_summary: All material outcomes of the task are satisfied with direct, coherent evidence: node1 runs a Kea DHCPv4 server on the shared private segment (eth1/10.10.10.1/24, pool .100-.200), and node2/node3 are confirmed to obtain their addresses on that segment dynamically via systemd-networkd DHCP rather than static configuration, both before and after a full restart cycle. The separately mandated node-restart evidence protocol is also fully satisfied for all three nodes, with baseline boot identity, disruption, changed boot identity, and recovered DHCP client/server state directly observed and cross-checked against the fixed lifecycle snapshots. Operational hygiene is high; the only imperfect commands were failed CLI syntax attempts during initial DHCP configuration authoring, which caused no persisted side effects.
limitations: The private-network DHCP relationship was validated functionally (leases, dynamic addressing) but no explicit end-to-end connectivity/ping test between node2/node3 over the 10.10.10.0/24 subnet was captured.
VyOS config.boot persistence after restart was confirmed via live interface/service state and lease table, but the raw saved config.boot file contents were not re-dumped post-restart.

operational_hygiene.summary: The command trace shows a normal iterative discovery-and-configure workflow: initial CLI syntax attempts on node1 failed (subnet-parameters/default-router paths invalid, missing subnet-id, a duplicate 'address already exists' notice) before the executor converged on the correct Kea-backed set commands; none of these failed attempts mutated persisted state (each failed 'commit' or 'set' either errored out or was a no-op, and the final successful commit+save is the only durable change). No stray files, failed services, weakened security controls, or unreverted troubleshooting residue were observed in the after_executor snapshot versus after_prepare — differences are limited to expected boot-identity churn, ephemeral systemd-private tmp dirs, new listening sockets for the Kea DHCP service, and DHCP client sockets on node2/node3, all directly attributable to the task and the restart protocol. All three restarts (node1, node2, node3) were single and directly tied to the mandated restart-evidence protocol.
